findings.title: Cron cancel loop aborts on first SendGrid error and defers all DB deletes until the end
findings.body: All SendGrid cancel calls and the `workflowReminder.delete` queries sit inside one try/catch. The delete queries are only awaited via `Promise.all` after the loop finishes. If any `client.request` throws (batch already sent, already cancelled, 4xx or 5xx), the catch swallows it. The remaining reminders are never cancelled, so those emails go out. The reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB because `Promise.all` is not reached. On the next run they are re-sent to SendGrid. If SendGrid rejects a cancel for an already-cancelled batch, the same failing reminder aborts the loop again and again. One bad record can therefore block every later cancellation until its `scheduledDate` passes. Handle each reminder in its own try/catch and delete (or flag) each row right after its successful cancel.

findings.title: `immediateDelete` path still uses the limited SendGrid cancel API, with no DB flag and no fallback
findings.body: The PR exists because SendGrid allows at most 100 pending cancellations. Yet `immediateDelete` still POSTs `status: cancel` straight to SendGrid. It is used for rescheduled bookings (handleNewBooking), deleted workflows and deleted steps. Reschedules and large workflow deletions can therefore still hit the 100-cancel cap. When the call fails, the error is only logged and the reminder is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted. The email is then sent anyway, which is the original bug. On success the row is also left untouched (not flagged, not deleted), so a later cancel or reschedule of the same booking sends a duplicate cancel for the same batch. For the reschedule case the booking and its reminders are retained, so simply setting `cancelled: true` (the deferred path) would avoid the limit. At minimum, fall back to `cancelled: true` when the immediate cancel fails.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget although the DB write is the only cancellation mechanism
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called inside `forEach` without being awaited. Previously the reminder DB deletions were collected and awaited in `Promise.all`. Now the DB update (`cancelled: true`) or delete is the only thing that stops the email, and nothing waits for it. In a serverless environment the work can be dropped once the response is sent, which silently reintroduces the 'reminder still sent for a cancelled booking' bug. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx (requestReschedule), handleNewBooking.ts and several places in workflows.tsx. Collect the promises and await them (e.g. add them to the `Promise.all`).

findings.title: Reschedule re-cancels reminders already cancelled by requestReschedule and ignores the `cancelled` flag
findings.body: When an organizer uses `requestReschedule`, the old booking's email reminders are only flagged `cancelled: true`. The attendee then books a new slot via handleNewBooking, which loads `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders`, including the already-flagged ones. For each of them it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` and sends a second SendGrid cancel for the same batch. That wastes pending-cancel slots and may error. Because the call is not awaited and errors are only logged, a failure leaves things unflagged. The loop should skip reminders where `cancelled` is already true. It should also prefer the deferred path (flag only) over the immediate SendGrid cancel.

findings.title: Cancellations made shortly before send time can be missed by the 15-minute cron
findings.body: A cancelled reminder is only handed to SendGrid when the cron runs within the hour before `scheduledDate`. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and a cancellation made after the last run before the send time is never processed. The first-step `deleteMany` then removes the row after the send time, and the email goes out for a cancelled or rescheduled booking. Likewise, any skipped or failed cron run in that window loses the cancellation. This is an inherent limitation of the deferred design and should at least be documented. A mitigation would be to cancel directly when the reminder is within the last 15 minutes, or to widen the window.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import and type-only symbols turned into value imports
findings.body: After removing `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]`, `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in this file but was added as a value import. `PrismaPromise` was also changed from `import type` to a regular value import although it is only used as a type. This produces an unused-import lint error. The same unnecessary `import type` to value-import change was made for `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput` and `Prisma` in handleNewBooking.ts. Restore the `import type` form.

findings.title: No tests for the new cancel flow or cron cancellation step
findings.body: The PR changes the cancellation contract of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (new signature, new `cancelled` column, new deferred cron step). It adds no tests for the deferred flag, the immediate path, the null-`referenceId` path, or the cron picking up `cancelled` reminders within the one-hour window. The previous fix (#6991) failed silently for the same lack of coverage.
